name: Kisan Credit Card (KCC)
tagline: Affordable institutional credit for crop cultivation and allied activities
whatItIs: A single-window credit facility providing farmers with timely and affordable institutional credit for crop cultivation and allied activities, including dairy, poultry, and fisheries, through a Kisan Credit Card (KCC).
benefits: Provides affordable short-term credit for seeds, fertilizer, and other input costs, as well as post-harvest expenses and household consumption needs. The effective 4% rate is dramatically lower than informal moneylender rates (often 24%+), preventing debt traps. It also covers investment credit for farm equipment, livestock, and allied infrastructure.
pros: Very low effective interest rate (4% per annum)
Single-window flexibility for both short-term working capital and investment credit
Covers allied activities like dairy, poultry, and fisheries
Wide network of 457 banks onboarded with over 7.7 crore active accounts
Collateral-free up to ₹2 lakh (up to ₹3 lakh with crop tie-up)
cons: The 3% prompt repayment incentive is forfeited if repayment is even one day late
Aadhaar linkage with bank account is compulsory
Small and marginal farmers may still find the application process document-heavy
keyLimitation: A government panel noted that tenant farmers and landless farmers (roughly 35-40% of all farmers) often struggle to access this scheme because they lack formal land records, pushing them back to informal lenders. To address this, NABARD has initiated CBDC-based pilots in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.

name: Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS)
tagline: Short-term working capital loan with prompt repayment interest relief
whatItIs: A short-term working capital loan scheme for crop cultivation and allied activities, accessed primarily through the Kisan Credit Card (KCC).
benefits: It provides affordable short-term credit for seeds, fertilizer, and other input costs. The effective 4% rate is dramatically lower than informal moneylender rates (often 24%+), preventing debt traps. The scheme also covers post-harvest storage against warehouse receipts, helping farmers avoid distress sales.
pros: Very low effective interest rate (4%) upon prompt repayment
Covers crop cultivation as well as allied activities like dairy and fisheries
Helps stabilize farmer incomes and protects against informal moneylenders
Includes post-harvest storage against negotiable warehouse receipts for up to 6 months
cons: Benefits are strictly capped at ₹3 lakh (₹2 lakh for allied-only)
You lose the 3% incentive if repayment is even one day late
Aadhaar linkage with bank account is compulsory
keyLimitation: A government panel has noted that tenant farmers and landless farmers (roughly 35-40% of all farmers) often struggle to access this scheme because they lack formal land records, pushing them back to informal lenders.

name: PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi)
tagline: ₹6,000 yearly income support paid in 3 equal instalments of ₹2,000
whatItIs: A central sector scheme launched in February 2019 to supplement the financial needs of landholding farmer families through direct income support of ₹6,000 per year, transferred in three equal instalments of ₹2,000 into Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).
benefits: It provides direct cash support to farmers for agricultural inputs like seeds, fertilizers, and pesticides, as well as household expenses such as education and medical costs. A NITI Aayog evaluation showed over 92% of beneficiaries used the assistance for essential agricultural inputs, and approximately 85% reported an increase in agricultural income.
pros: Direct benefit transfer (DBT) directly into bank account eliminates intermediaries and leakage
Significant scale with over 9.49 crore beneficiaries in the 23rd instalment
Women farmers have received more than ₹1.06 lakh crore (nearly 1 in 4 beneficiaries)
Extended till 2030-31 with a robust ₹3.15 lakh crore outlay
100% grant funding — no loan repayment required
cons: The amount has remained fixed at ₹6,000 since inception in 2019 despite inflation
Digital divide leaves some eligible farmers excluded due to online portal difficulties
Payments blocked for over 73 lakh beneficiaries due to pending mandatory requirements (land seeding, Aadhaar seeding, e-KYC)
keyLimitation: Farmer leaders have noted that ₹6,000 a year is a 'token gesture' that doesn't solve structural farm problems. Thousands of eligible farmers remain excluded due to digital barriers, and parliamentary committees have questioned why payout hasn't adjusted for inflation.

name: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF)
tagline: Medium-to-long term debt up to ₹2 Crore with 3% interest subvention
whatItIs: A medium-to-long-term debt financing facility for building post-harvest infrastructure like warehouses, cold storage, silos, sorting/grading units, and primary processing units.
benefits: It helps farmers add value to their produce. Instead of selling raw crops at low prices during harvest glut, they can store, process, and market them strategically. This reduces the 15-20% post-harvest losses in India and lets farmers capture more of the final consumer price.
pros: Large loan ceiling of up to ₹2 crore per eligible project
Significant 3% per annum interest subvention on the loan
Credit guarantee coverage under CGTMSE solves the collateral problem for up to ₹2 crore
Supports a wide range of infrastructure from packhouses to custom hiring centers
cons: The ₹2 crore cap is considered insufficient for large projects like complete cold chain networks
Working capital is not covered, leading to temporarily underutilized assets
Awareness among local bank branch officials is low, causing approval delays
keyLimitation: Active demand from farmer organizations to raise the subvention ceiling to ₹5 crore. Lack of working capital financing within the fund restricts newly built facilities until operations stabilize.

name: Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF)
tagline: Up to 90% project cost with 3% interest subvention & 2-year moratorium
whatItIs: A specialized fund for medium-to-long-term debt to build processing and value-addition infrastructure in the dairy, meat, and animal feed sectors.
benefits: This scheme encourages investment in value addition. By setting up dairy or meat processing units, it creates an organized market for milk and meat, improving price realization for farmers. It also generates rural employment and builds essential cold-chain and animal feed processing capacity.
pros: No upper limit on the loan amount for large-scale enterprise projects
Long 8-year interest subvention period of 3% per annum
High financing coverage of up to 90% of total project cost
2-year moratorium on principal repayment provides essential breathing room
25% credit guarantee coverage for MSME category projects
cons: It is exclusively a term loan, not meant for working capital
Focus is on processing infrastructure, so small farmers may not benefit directly unless grouped into an FPO
Application process requires a comprehensive Detailed Project Report (DPR) and is relatively complex
keyLimitation: High documentation and techno-economic appraisal hurdles make it difficult for grassroots smallholder farmers to access without professional consultancy or FPO federations.

name: PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME)
tagline: Upgrade a small food-processing unit with bank credit and subsidy support
whatItIs: A credit-linked subsidy programme that helps individual micro food-processing units, SHGs, FPOs and cooperatives upgrade equipment, packaging, branding and quality systems.
benefits: The subsidy reduces the effective project burden while a bank loan finances eligible machinery and business improvements. It is useful for farmer groups that want to process their own crops instead of selling only raw produce.
pros: Credit-linked subsidy of 35% of eligible project cost, subject to the scheme ceiling
Supports individual units as well as SHGs, FPOs and cooperatives
Helps improve value realisation, packaging and market access
cons: Applicant must contribute a share of the project cost
Loan approval and subsidy release depend on bank appraisal and scheme verification
A viable food-processing project and applicable licences are required
keyLimitation: The support is for eligible micro food-processing projects, not unrestricted cash or crop cultivation expenses. Confirm current application windows and eligible products with the district nodal agency.

name: PM-KUSUM
tagline: Reduce irrigation costs with a subsidised solar pump and bank finance
whatItIs: A renewable-energy support scheme covering decentralised solar plants, stand-alone solar agriculture pumps and solarisation of existing grid-connected pumps.
benefits: The combined subsidy and institutional finance can reduce the upfront cost of solar irrigation, lower diesel or electricity expenses and improve irrigation reliability. Farmers may also earn from surplus power where the state implementation model allows it.
pros: Central and state assistance can substantially reduce the farmer contribution
Cuts recurring diesel or grid-electricity costs for irrigation
Can be implemented for individual farmers, cooperatives and farmer groups
cons: Availability, subsidy share and beneficiary selection vary by state
The farmer must arrange the remaining contribution or loan amount
Pump capacity, land records and grid connectivity conditions apply
keyLimitation: PM-KUSUM is implemented through state agencies and approved vendors, so the exact subsidy, loan terms and application route must be checked with the state renewable-energy or agriculture department.

name: FPO Credit Guarantee Scheme
tagline: Help Farmer Producer Organisations access working capital and term loans

subLimits.creditGuaranteeCoverage: As per eligible lender and scheme norms

whatItIs: Credit guarantee support that makes it easier for eligible Farmer Producer Organisations and producer groups to obtain collateral-light working capital and investment loans from banks.
benefits: The guarantee reduces lender risk, helping farmer organisations finance aggregation, storage, input supply, transport, processing and marketing. Members can access stronger institutional credit by applying through their FPO rather than individually.
pros: Improves access to bank credit when an FPO has limited collateral
Can support both working capital and business infrastructure
Encourages collective purchase, storage and sale of farm produce
cons: Only a registered and properly governed producer organisation can apply
The guarantee does not remove repayment responsibility or bank appraisal
Audited accounts, resolutions and a viable business plan are normally required
keyLimitation: Guarantee coverage, eligible borrower limits and fees depend on the active government or lender guidelines. The FPO should confirm terms with a participating bank or the relevant implementing agency.

name: National Livestock Mission (NLM) Entrepreneurship Development
tagline: Start or expand a sheep, goat, piggery, poultry or feed enterprise
whatItIs: An entrepreneurship support programme that combines bank finance with capital subsidy for eligible livestock, poultry, piggery, sheep and goat, and feed or fodder enterprises.
benefits: It helps farmers diversify beyond crop income and build income-generating livestock infrastructure. The subsidy can reduce the project cost while the bank loan covers the balance, subject to technical appraisal.
pros: Supports multiple livestock and feed enterprise models
Capital subsidy can reduce the amount financed by the promoter
Suitable for individual entrepreneurs, SHGs and FPO-linked projects
cons: Beneficiary contribution and bank appraisal are required
Projects need technical planning, animal-health arrangements and market linkage
Subsidy release follows implementation and verification conditions
keyLimitation: The applicable subsidy ceiling and eligible activities can change with programme guidelines and state implementation. Obtain the current project list from the state animal-husbandry department before borrowing.
